title: Meridian — Class A Business Campus
description: Meridian is a class A business campus template: pinned full-bleed panels, numbered chapters, oversized numerals and a dark-light rhythm.

intro.lede: A class A business campus on the city's western rim. Bold geometry and honest engineering give growing companies a launch pad, not just a lease.

heading: Confident ideas.
Louder ambitions.
idea.statement: Meridian reads as sculpture first and floor plate second. The campus resets the skyline of its district and hands every tenant a share of that signal.

location.heading: Location
location.intro: The campus anchors a corridor where the city is spending heavily on transit and public space, so the neighbourhood compounds in value while you work.

title: Minutes from
the runway
slides.text: Catch a morning flight without an alarm-clock tragedy: the airport door is a short drive from the lobby turnstiles.

title: A widening
road grid
slides.text: Two arterials and a new interchange put the centre of town within a coffee's worth of driving.

title: Homes within
walking range
slides.text: Dense new housing sits one stop away, so the commute can be a stroll rather than a schedule.

accessibility.statement: Nearer than the map suggests. Meridian sits against the orbital exit, so drivers skip the morning crush and cyclists ride a dedicated greenway the whole way in.

heading: Green space for people
who never sit still
slides: Three public parks ring the campus with trail loops, open lawns and water you can actually reach on a lunch break.
Winter swaps the trails for groomed ski tracks and a lit skating oval five minutes from the lobby doors.
Prefer culture to cardio? A concert shell and two galleries share the same block as your badge reader.

architecture.heading: Architecture
architecture.intro: Three stepped volumes share a plinth and lean into the avenue, a silhouette built to be recognised at highway speed.
slides: Parts of the massing float above the plaza on slender columns, opening the ground floor to daylight.
Vertical fins pace the façade and stretch the eye upward, giving the block its sense of motion.
A glass base with double-height storefronts keeps the street level open and light.
Selective glazing tempers the sun without stealing the view.
After dark, programmed façade lighting redraws the building in thin bright strokes.

lobby.heading: Lobby
lobby.intro: Independent entrance halls, each with its own reception desk and waiting lounge, mean visitors never queue behind another company's morning rush.
lobby.statement: The interiors follow one quiet rule: muted materials, generous voids, and daylight doing most of the decorating.
lobby.detail: Custom joinery and a restrained palette keep the halls calm at nine in the morning and composed at nine at night.

offices.heading: Offices
offices.intro: Tenants are the campus's whole point. Column-free spans, raised floors and operable partitions let a team of twelve become a team of eighty without moving out.
slides: Clear heights up to 5,4 meters with full-height glazing keep even the deepest desk in daylight.

comfort.statement: Comfort that guards the workday. Meridian keeps the background hum of running a building away from the people doing the work, quietly and around the clock.

cards.title: Service without ceremony
cards.text: One flat service package covers the essentials, with no surprise line items at quarter end.

cards.title: An operator on call
cards.text: A resident app and a staffed desk resolve the small stuff before it becomes a ticket chain.

engineering.heading: Systems
engineering.intro: The building runs itself: ventilation, heating, access and metering are automated end to end and watched from one control room.
engineering.detail: Climate systems hold each floor at its own setpoint and refresh the air on a schedule tuned to occupancy, not habit.

infrastructure.heading: Amenities
infrastructure.intro: Meridian is more than desks. The plinth carries a working high street, so errands happen between meetings instead of after hours.
infrastructure.note: These ground floors are meant to pull the whole district in, not just the badge-holders upstairs.
infrastructure.courtText: The inner court is furnished for actual work: long tables, weatherproof power and shade that moves with the sun.

cards.title: Concept and massing
cards.text: Halden Bureau shaped the three volumes and the plinth. Their portfolio runs from transit halls to quiet chapels, and it shows in the section.

cards.title: Light planning
cards.text: Studio Lucent drew the night façade and the lobby light plot, work that has picked up two international lighting awards.

cards.title: Common interiors
cards.text: Atelier Marlow furnished the halls and courtyards, keeping the palette calm so the architecture does the talking.

footer.footnote: Everything on this page is placeholder marketing copy for a design template; no real building, offer or contract stands behind it.
